producer_report.summary: Added a code check that compares a job's changed files with a stored list of allowed paths. It runs after each producer report and again at the head of check_and_verify, before the decision gate, the CI push and the verifier. When an accepted criterion limits which files may change (matched by the new `limits_changed_files` in briefs.rs), the job record stores `allowed_paths` as the reading's deliverable paths, with a leading ./ removed and duplicates dropped. The new field is optional on `Job`, with the same serde attributes as `dispatch_branch`, so older records still parse. The check (`outside_allowed_paths`) compares normalised paths, deleted files included. A stored entry ending in `/` covers its directory tree. An outside file is sent back to the producer with each path named, the criterion quoted and an instruction to revert it (`send_back_text_scoped`). It has its own one extra send-back, so an outside change made after the first send-back is sent back again (up to three producer runs, only for a job with a stored list). A diff still outside at the head of check_and_verify closes the job as Failed with a `SCOPE_REASON_PREFIX` reason before the checks and the verifier. The same check catches a resumed candidate that skipped the loop. `retry_findings` carries that reason to the next producer. Jobs with no stored list and nested runs are not checked. The dispatch output gains a `scope` line when a list is stored. CHANGELOG.md and the athena.job/1 row of docs/records.md are updated. The full suite passed at the end (`cargo test --locked`, exit 0).

open_issues: Departures from the plan, all minor: reading.rs needed no 'allowed_paths: None' on its Job stubs, because they use ..dispatched_job_stub() from JSON. run/producer.rs, store.rs and docs/records.md changed although they are not in the reading's deliverables: the loop lives in producer.rs, store.rs holds a Job fixture that needs the new field, and records.md gets one clause on the athena.job/1 row. If the verifier treats the docs/records.md clause as scope creep, that is the one file to revert.

Test D from the plan (a nested run is not checked) has no end-to-end test. The skip is in the code (`self.nested.is_none()` in producer_loop's scope selection and in check_and_verify) and I did not drive a nested run.

Open questions from the plan are still for the user: whether the extra scope-only send-back (up to 3 producer runs for a job with a stored list) is wanted, and whether files a build always rewrites, such as Cargo.lock, should be allowed for a limited job. As built, any changed file outside the deliverables, and not under a 'dir/' deliverable, is flagged.
The matcher is deliberately narrow: bare 'test-only', and 'test-only edits', do not match. A limiting criterion in other words is not checked, as today, and the verifier is still the backstop.
An older Athena binary reading a job.json that has allowed_paths would fail on the unknown key (deny_unknown_fields). The key is written only for a limited job.
mistakes: My first draft of the matcher counted words after turning every non-alphanumeric character into a space, so a path like crates/a.rs became three words and 'only crates/a.rs and README.md may be changed' fell outside the 6-word window. I switched to whitespace-separated words with edge punctuation trimmed and a hyphen as a word break.
I wrote a test string containing the banned word 'hand-off' and reworded it before running the policy scan.
A first test assertion expected the outside paths in producer-write order; the change list is path-sorted. Fixed the assertion.
learnings: producer_loop lives in crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs, not run/mod.rs. The send-back limit and break condition are there, so the in-loop check could not go in mod.rs.

Job struct literals exist only in run/mod.rs, store.rs (a test fixture) and records.rs (a test). reading.rs builds Jobs from JSON stubs with ..dispatched_job_stub(), so it needed no allowed_paths: None.

A retry's reading is refused unless it lists the earlier job's changed files as deliverables or puts them in out_of_scope (reading refusal: 'leaves out the earlier job's files'). The resume test's fake reader therefore adds NOTES.md to out_of_scope on its second call.
The change list that comes back from change_list() is ordered by path (EXTRA.md before NOTES.md), so the outside paths in messages follow that order, not the order the producer wrote the files.
The policy scan rejects the word hand-off. A test string with it had to be reworded.
desires: A way to read a background command's output file from inside the working directory; the full suite exceeded the 20-minute foreground limit here (other cargo runs were sharing the build lock), and I could only wait for the completion notice.
A sleep or wait primitive, so I could wait for a background run without running unrelated commands.
